kjv: in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed
mine: by your offspring all the nations of the earth shall bless themselves
note: As in 22:18 the verb is hithpael (hitbarakhu), most naturally reflexive ("bless themselves by", i.e. invoke as a model of blessing); the KJV takes it as passive with the LXX. Context: bless themselves, i.e. invoke Abraham's offspring as a model of blessing (medium confidence). The verb is hithpael here and at 22:18 (niphal at 12:3, 18:18, 28:14); Gen 48:20 shows the idiom: 'By you Israel will pronounce blessings, saying, God make you like Ephraim'.
Hebrew metsaheq (the Isaac wordplay again) here denotes conjugal fondling that showed she was his wife; "sporting" now suggests merely playing.

kjv: might lightly have lien with thy wife
mine: might easily have lain with your wife
note: Hebrew kim'at, "almost, easily"; KJV "lightly" meant easily, but a modern reader may take it as "casually".
Hebrew merea, "companion, friend", appears to be a court title ("the king's friend", cf. 2 Sam 15:37); the KJV "one of his friends" also needlessly adds "one of".
